links.outcome: Model performance and false negative rate by gender subgroup
links.effect: FNR was 0.082 for female vs 0.005 for male samples; accuracy was lower for female samples across all models (worst case 0.844 vs 0.913).
links.quote: Our results revealed concerning predictive performance differences, with substantially higher false negative rates (FNRs) for female samples (FNR=0.082) compared with male samples (FNR=0.005).

links.outcome: Effect of bias mitigation algorithms on gender disparities in FNR and accuracy
links.effect: Reweighting gave the best FNR ratio (4.636 to 2.591) but raised male FNR and reduced male accuracy; disparities mitigated but not eliminated; some methods no better than original.
links.quote: The results showed that, even when disparities can be mitigated with most of the algorithms, they cannot be eliminated.

links.effect: Aggregate balanced accuracy was >87% with FNR 4-6%, but decomposing by gender showed FNR roughly twice as high for females and lower accuracy for females.
links.quote: Nevertheless, we observed important performance differences when decomposing such values by gender, yielding in the worst case (MLP classifier, 1 model per gender) an accuracy of 0.913 for male samples and 0.844 for female samples (relative difference of 8% accuracy).

links.outcome: Human annotator performance differences by gender against ground truth
links.effect: Labelers had higher accuracy and lower FNR for male samples (4 of 5 labelers); Cohen kappa 0.807 female vs 0.841 male, suggesting annotator bias in the reference standard.
links.quote: As shown in Figure 6 , the obtained results show that labelers had greater performance for male samples, with higher accuracy and lower FNR.
